items.stem: What is the right relationship between automated PR review and human review?

options.text: Automated review assists; a human stays accountable for the merge
options.rationale: Correct: automation supports review but does not replace human judgement.

options.text: Automated review fully replaces human review
options.rationale: Automation misses judgement and context a human provides.

options.text: Human review is unnecessary once a bot is enabled
options.rationale: A bot cannot own accountability for a merge.

options.text: Both can be skipped if tests pass
options.rationale: Tests do not cover design, security and context review.

items.explanation: Correct: automation supports review but does not replace human judgement.

items.stem: Which TWO habits keep automated review valuable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Tune the reviewer to reduce noise
options.rationale: Correct: a noisy reviewer gets ignored, hiding real issues.

options.text: Verify a suggested fix actually resolves the finding
options.rationale: Correct: suggested fixes must be checked, not applied blindly.

options.text: Treat review as a box to tick
options.rationale: A rubber-stamp gate adds no quality.

items.explanation: Correct: a noisy reviewer gets ignored, hiding real issues.

items.stem: The review bot produces so many low-value flags that developers ignore it. What should you do?

options.text: Tune what it flags so real issues stand out
options.rationale: Correct: reducing noise restores the signal developers act on.
Removing human review makes the problem worse.
Ignoring findings defeats the purpose of review.

options.text: Accept that review no longer adds value
options.rationale: The fix is tuning, not abandoning review.

items.explanation: Correct: reducing noise restores the signal developers act on.
